Tessera is a Linux gaming OS (an image built on Bazzite/Fedora with bootc) with a Qt (QML) launcher UI running a Node main process.
Pay particular attention to:
- The launcher's main process (system_files/usr/lib/tessera/launcher/main/*.js) handles requests from
  its page over IPC. Every request is checked for its sender (main/ipcGuard.js); handlers must
  validate every field, and anything privileged must require the admin PIN (pinLock.pinOk) and,
  for Guest, guestDenies(). Flag handlers that trust input from the screen, paths that can escape the
  Tessera folder, and new privileged operations without the PIN check.
- Programs are started with execFile/spawn and argument lists, never a shell.
- Root-run scripts (system_files/usr/libexec/tessera/*, usr/bin/*) and the systemd units and polkit
  rule (usr/share/polkit-1/rules.d/49-tessera-update.rules) that let the console start them:
  arguments must be fixed or whitelisted; nothing a user controls may reach a root command.
- The boot menu (usr/share/tessera/grub/*.cfg, GRUB script) must never skip a password or the
  admin PIN, and must leave GRUB's failed-update fallback alone.
- Renderer code must not build HTML from text that came from outside (game titles, web pages,
  add-ons, Wi-Fi names); index.html's Content-Security-Policy must stay strict.
- Add-on packages and signatures (addon-package.js, addon-verify.js): nothing unsigned may be
  treated as Official; unpacking must refuse links, unsafe names and oversized content.
- Secrets: the add-on signing key must never be in the repository or in CI.
